hints: Convert the given wavelength to metres: $2\text{ cm} = 0.02\text{ m}$ and compare it with visible light at about $5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$.
Recall the order of the electromagnetic spectrum by wavelength: X-ray, optical, microwave, radio.
Check whether $0.02\text{ m}$ fits the microwave band of about $1\text{ mm}$ to $10\text{ cm}$ rather than the much longer radio band.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: the telescope detects radiation of wavelength $\lambda = 2\text{ cm} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m} = 0.02\text{ m}$.
Recall the approximate wavelength ranges: X-rays $\sim 10^{-10}\text{ m}$, optical $\sim 10^{-7}\text{ m}$, microwaves $\sim 10^{-3}\text{ m}$ to $10^{-1}\text{ m}$, radio waves $> 10^{-1}\text{ m}$.
Compare $0.02\text{ m}$ with these ranges: it is much larger than optical and X-ray wavelengths but shorter than typical long radio waves.
Note that $0.02\text{ m}$ lies inside the $1\text{ mm}$ to $10\text{ cm}$ microwave band, between infrared and radio.
Therefore the instrument detecting $2\text{ cm}$ radiation is a microwave telescope. This is option A.

options.A: A wavelength of $2\text{ cm}$ or $0.02\text{ m}$ lies in the microwave region between infrared and radio waves.
options.B: Optical light has wavelengths around $400$ to $700\text{ nm}$, which is about $10^7$ times smaller than $2\text{ cm}$.
options.C: Radio waves are longer than microwaves, typically greater than about $10\text{ cm}$, so $2\text{ cm}$ is too short.
options.D: X-rays have wavelengths around $10^{-10}\text{ m}$, which is far shorter than $2\text{ cm}$.
